name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

298:{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-07-24T18:30:47.812697+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "Bash", "data": {"content": "# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge

A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
integral curve over a field.  The project follows the Picard-scheme route: it
constructs the relative Picard functor, represents it through the
Grassmannian/Quot/flattening-stratification machinery, identifies its identity
component as an abelian variety of dimension equal to the genus, and proves the
Albanese universal property.

This is the workspace's ambitious Picard-scheme route. It is developed alongside
`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which follows a separate curve-specialized strategy.

The formalization is advanced but incomplete.  The live Horizon roadmap
separates the completed infrastructure from the remaining flat-base-change,
Serre-finiteness, Quot, Picard, Picard-identity-component, and Albanese cones.

## Navigation

- [`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian.lean): project import root.
- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): final Jacobian witness
  interface and assembly point.
- [`blueprint/web/index.html`](blueprint/web/index.html): generated mathematical blueprint.
- [`../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md):
  the alternative Rebuild route.
- `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.jacobian`: current nested completion roadmap.

## Layout

- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/`: sheaf cohomology, the finite-cover Cech
  complex, higher direct images, and flat base change.
- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard
  functor, Grassmannians, Quot schemes, flattening stratification, and Picard
  identity components.
- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/`: rigidity and extension of rational maps, plus
  the Albanese factorization.
- `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/`: divisor and adelic Riemann--Roch
  infrastructure.
- `blueprint/src/chapters/`: the mathematical blueprint.
- `hgraph/`: the generated statement/declaration dependency graph.
- [`../../references/summary.md`](../../references/summary.md): shared source
  bibliography and retrieval notes.

## Build

The project uses Lean `v4.31.0` and Mathlib `v4.31.0`.

```bash
lake exe cache get
lake build
```

This project is part of an Archon Horizon workspace.  Roadmap, task, inbox, and
cross-project state live at the workspace root and are accessed through the
`horizon` CLI.

  2026	/-- **(I) Ring-iso-semilinear `IsLocalizedModule` transport.** Given a ring isomorphism
  2027	`σ : R ≃+* R'`, two `σ`-semilinear additive isomorphisms `e₁ : M₁ ≃+ N₁`, `e₂ : M₂ ≃+ N₂` (i.e.

  2036	    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
  2037	    [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module R' N₁] [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R' N₂]
  2038	    (S : Submonoid R)
  2039	    (g : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) [IsLocalizedModule S g]
  2040	    (e₁ : M₁ ≃+ N₁) (e₂ : M₂ ≃+ N₂)

   648	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — annihilator under localization
   649	
   650	The annihilator ideal sheaf `def:modules_annihilator` of a coherent sheaf is
   651	built from the affine-local data `U ↦ Ann_{O(U)}(F(U))`, packaged as a
   652	`Scheme.IdealSheafData`. The structure's coherence field `map_ideal_basicOpen`
   653	requires the algebraic fact that, for a *finitely generated* module, the
   654	annihilator commutes with localization:
   655	`Ann(S⁻¹M) = (Ann M)·S⁻¹R`. Mathlib (at the pinned commit) does not carry this
   656	lemma, so it is supplied here as the load-bearing engine for that construction.
   657	-/
   658	
   659	namespace Module
   660	
   661	/-- For a finitely generated module `M` over a commutative ring `R`, the
   662	annihilator commutes with localization: if `Rₚ` localizes `R` at a submonoid
   663	`S` and `f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ` localizes `M` at `S`, then the annihilator of `Mₚ`
   664	over `Rₚ` is the extension (`Ideal.map` along `algebraMap R Rₚ`) of the
   665	annihilator of `M` over `R`.
   666	
   667	This is the abstract `IsLocalization`/`IsLocalizedModule` form, matching the
   668	shape needed for the affine-basic-open coherence of the annihilator ideal sheaf
   669	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.annihilator`, `def:modules_annihilator`):
   670	the structure-sheaf restriction `Γ(X,U) → Γ(X, D(f))` is
   671	`IsLocalization (powers f)`, and for a quasi-coherent `F` the section
   672	restriction is `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)`.
   673	
   674	Mathlib has no annihilator-localization lemma, so this is project-local. -/
   675	theorem annihilator_isLocalizedModule_eq_map
   676	    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R)
   677	    {Rₚ : Type*} [CommRing Rₚ] [Algebra R Rₚ] [IsLocalization S Rₚ]
   678	    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
   679	    {Mₚ : Type*} [AddCommGroup Mₚ] [Module R Mₚ] [Module Rₚ Mₚ] [IsScalarTower R Rₚ Mₚ]
   680	    (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ) [IsLocalizedModule S f] :
   681	    Module.annihilator Rₚ Mₚ = (Module.annihilator R M).map (algebraMap R Rₚ) := by
   682	  classical
   683	  obtain ⟨t, htop⟩ := (Module.Finite.fg_top (R := R) (M := M))
   684	  -- annihilating a spanning finset suffices for membership in the annihilator
   685	  have key : ∀ (r : R), (∀ m ∈ t, r • m = 0) → r ∈ Module.annihilator R M := by
   686	    intro r h
   687	    rw [Module.mem_annihilator]
   688	    intro x
   689	    have hx : x ∈ Submodule.span R (t : Set M) := htop ▸ Submodule.mem_top
   690	    induction hx using Submodule.span_induction with
   691	    | mem y hy => exact h y hy
   692	    | zero => simp
   693	    | add a b _ _ ha hb => rw [smul_add, ha, hb, add_zero]
   694	    | smul c a _ ha => rw [smul_comm, ha, smul_zero]
   695	  apply le_antisymm
   696	  · -- `Ann Rₚ Mₚ ⊆ (Ann R M).map`: clear one common denominator over the generators
   697	    intro y hy
   698	    rw [Module.mem_annihilator] at hy
   699	    obtain ⟨⟨a, s⟩, rfl⟩ := IsLocalization.mk'_surjective S y
   700	    dsimp only at hy ⊢
   701	    have hgen : ∀ m ∈ t, ∃ u : S, (u : R) • a • m = 0 := by
   702	      intro m hm
   703	      have hz := hy (IsLocalizedModule.mk' f m (1 : S))
   704	      rw [IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk' Rₚ f, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_eq_zero,
   705	        IsLocalizedModule.eq_zero_iff S f] at hz
   706	      obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hz
   707	      exact ⟨u, hu⟩
   708	    choose u hu using hgen
   709	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ : ∃ U : S, ∀ m ∈ t, (U : R) • a • m = 0 := by
   710	      refine ⟨∏ x ∈ t.attach, u x.1 x.2, ?_⟩
   711	      intro m hm
   712	      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ :=
   713	        Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem (fun x : t => u x.1 x.2) (Finset.mem_attach t ⟨m, hm⟩)
   714	      have hcoe : ((∏ x ∈ t.attach, u x.1 x.2 : S) : R) = (u m hm : R) * (c : R) := by
   715	        rw [hc]; push_cast; ring
   716	      rw [hcoe, mul_smul, smul_comm, hu m hm, smul_zero]
   717	    have hUa : (U : R) * a ∈ Module.annihilator R M := by
   718	      apply key; intro m hm; rw [mul_smul]; exact hU m hm
   719	    have heq : IsLocalization.mk' Rₚ a s
   720	        = (algebraMap R Rₚ ((U : R) * a)) * IsLocalization.mk' Rₚ 1 (U * s) := by
   721	      rw [← IsLocalization.mk'_eq_mul_mk'_one, IsLocalization.mk'_eq_iff_eq]
   722	      push_cast; ring
   723	    rw [heq]
   724	    exact Ideal.mul_mem_right _ _ (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hUa)
   725	  · -- `(Ann R M).map ⊆ Ann Rₚ Mₚ`: the image of an annihilator annihilates
   726	    rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
   727	    intro a ha
   728	    rw [Ideal.mem_comap, Module.mem_annihilator]
   729	    rw [Module.mem_annihilator] at ha
   730	    intro x
   731	    obtain ⟨⟨m, s⟩, rfl⟩ := IsLocalizedModule.mk'_surjective S f x
   732	    dsimp only [Function.uncurry]
   733	    rw [← IsLocalization.mk'_one (M := S) Rₚ a, IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk' Rₚ f, ha m,
   734	      IsLocalizedModule.mk'_zero]
   735	
   736	end Module

   738	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — quasi-coherent sections localize on a basic open
   739	
   740	This section builds, bottom-up, toward the keystone
   741	`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`: for a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules `M`
   742	on a scheme `X`, an affine open `U`, and `f ∈ Γ(X,U)`, the restriction
   743	`M(U) → M(D(f))` exhibits `M(D(f))` as `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` over `Γ(X,U)`.
   744	
   745	The substance is the affine (Spec-local) computation: over `Spec R`, a quasi-coherent
   746	sheaf is `Ñ = tilde N` for `N = Γ(M)`, and the basic-open restriction of `Ñ` is the
   747	module localization map. Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.tilde` namespace already carries
   748	the localization fact for `tilde N` *as the map out of `N`* (the instance
   749	`IsLocalizedModule (.powers f) (tilde.toOpen N (basicOpen f)).hom`). The first building
   750	block below repackages this as a statement about the *presheaf restriction map* of `Ñ`
   751	itself (from global sections to `D(f)`), which is the form the downstream scheme-level
   752	argument consumes after the affine identification `M|_U ≅ Ñ`.
   753	
   754	Mathlib (at the pinned commit) does **not** prove that an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf
   755	on `Spec R` lies in the essential image of `tilde` (the comment in
   756	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Tilde.lean` says this "will later be shown"); the
   757	equivalence `QCoh(Spec R) ≃ Mod R` is a genuine gap. Consequently the keystone for an
   758	*arbitrary* quasi-coherent `M` is gated on that bridge (`IsQuasicoherent M → IsIso
   759	M.fromTildeΓ`); the building blocks here are stated for `tilde N` directly, and for a
   760	general `M : (Spec R).Modules` under the explicit hypothesis `[IsIso M.fromTildeΓ]`
   761	(equivalently, `M` in the essential image of `tilde`). -/
   762	
   763	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   764	
   765	open CategoryTheory Limits
   766	
   767	/-- **Basic-open restriction of a `tilde` sheaf is a module localization.**
   768	
   769	For `N : ModuleCat R` and `f : R`, the presheaf restriction map of the associated sheaf
   770	`Ñ = tilde N` from global sections `Γ(Ñ, ⊤)` to the basic open `Γ(Ñ, D(f))` exhibits the
   771	latter as `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` over `R`.
   772	
   773	This is the affine, Spec-local heart of `lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`. Mathlib
   774	carries the localization fact for the map `tilde.toOpen N (D f) : N → Γ(Ñ, D(f))` out of
   775	`N`; since `tilde.toOpen N ⊤ : N → Γ(Ñ, ⊤)` is an isomorphism and
   776	`tilde.toOpen N (D f) = tilde.toOpen N ⊤ ≫ restriction` (`tilde.toOpen_res`), precomposing
   777	the localization map with the inverse isomorphism (`IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv_right`)
   778	transfers the property to the restriction map. Project-local: Mathlib states the fact only
   779	for the map out of `N`, not for the presheaf restriction of `Ñ`. -/
   780	theorem isLocalizedModule_tilde_restrict {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (f : R) :
   781	    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f)
   782	      ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj (tilde N)).presheaf.map
   783	        (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op).hom := by
   784	  set res := (modulesSpecToSheaf.obj (tilde N)).presheaf.map
   785	        (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op with hresdef
   786	  have hres := tilde.toOpen_res N ⊤ (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)
   787	    (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤))
   788	  -- `e : N ≃ₗ Γ(Ñ, ⊤)` is the global-sections isomorphism of the tilde sheaf.
   789	  set e : N ≃ₗ[R] _ := (tilde.isoTop N).toLinearEquiv with hedef
   790	  have key : (tilde.toOpen N (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)).hom = res.hom ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap := by
   791	    rw [hedef, ← hres]; rfl
   792	  have hinst0 : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f)
   793	      (tilde.toOpen N (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)).hom := inferInstance
   794	  rw [key] at hinst0
   795	  set g := res.hom ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap with hg
   796	  haveI : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) g := hinst0
   797	  have h2 := IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv_right (S := Submonoid.powers f) (f := g) e.symm
   798	  have he : g ∘ₗ e.symm.toLinearMap = res.hom := by
   799	    apply LinearMap.ext; intro x
   800	    change res.hom (e (e.symm x)) = res.hom x
   801	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply]
   802	  rw [he] at h2
   803	  exact h2
   804	
   805	/-- **Basic-open restriction localizes, for a sheaf in the essential image of `tilde`.**
   806	
   807	For a sheaf of modules `M` on `Spec R` whose tilde-Gamma counit `M.fromTildeΓ` is an
   808	isomorphism (equivalently, `M` lies in the essential image of the `tilde` functor — the
   809	honest Spec-affine stand-in for quasi-coherence, see the section header), the presheaf
   810	restriction map of `M` from global sections `Γ(M, ⊤)` to the basic open `Γ(M, D(f))`
   811	exhibits the latter as `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` over `R`.

   813	This transports `isLocalizedModule_tilde_restrict` across the isomorphism
   814	`M.fromTildeΓ : tilde N ⟶ M` (where `N = Γ(M, ⊤)`): the induced presheaf isomorphism is
   815	natural in the open, so on each of `⊤` and `D(f)` it provides an `R`-linear isomorphism
   816	intertwining the two restriction maps. Post- and pre-composing the localization map for
   817	`tilde N` with these isomorphisms (`IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv`,
   818	`IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv_right`) yields the property for `M`.

   820	Project-local: it is the affine engine of `lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`. The
   821	general quasi-coherent case additionally requires the (currently Mathlib-absent) bridge
   822	`IsQuasicoherent M → IsIso M.fromTildeΓ`. -/
   823	theorem isLocalizedModule_restrict_of_isIso_fromTildeΓ {R : CommRingCat.{u}}
   824	    (M : (Spec R).Modules) [IsIso M.fromTildeΓ] (f : R) :
   825	    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f)
   826	      ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M).presheaf.map
   827	        (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op).hom := by
   828	  -- the presheaf-level isomorphism induced by the (iso) counit `M.fromTildeΓ`
   829	  let ψ := (TopCat.Sheaf.forget (ModuleCat R) (Spec R)).map (modulesSpecToSheaf.map M.fromTildeΓ)
   830	  haveI : IsIso ψ := inferInstance
   831	  haveI : IsIso (ψ.app (.op (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))) := inferInstance
   832	  haveI : IsIso (ψ.app (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))) := inferInstance
   833	  -- the component isomorphisms as `R`-linear equivalences

   835	  let eDf : _ ≃ₗ[R] _ := (asIso (ψ.app (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)))).toLinearEquiv
   836	  -- the restriction map of `tilde N` (localizes by `isLocalizedModule_tilde_restrict`)
   837	  let rt := ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj
   838	        (tilde ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M).presheaf.obj (.op ⊤)))).presheaf.map
   839	        (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op).hom
   840	  -- naturality square of `ψ` for `D(f) ⟶ ⊤`
   841	  have hnat := ψ.naturality (homOfLE (le_top : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⊤)).op
   842	  have hnathom := congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom hnat
   843	  rw [ModuleCat.hom_comp, ModuleCat.hom_comp] at hnathom
   844	  haveI hrt : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) rt :=
   845	    isLocalizedModule_tilde_restrict ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M).presheaf.obj (.op ⊤)) f
   846	  haveI step1 : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) (eDf.toLinearMap ∘ₗ rt) :=
   847	    IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv (S := Submonoid.powers f) (f := rt) (e := eDf)
   848	  haveI step2 : IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f)
   849	      ((eDf.toLinearMap ∘ₗ rt) ∘ₗ eTop.symm.toLinearMap) :=
   850	    IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv_right (S := Submonoid.powers f)
   851	      (f := eDf.toLinearMap ∘ₗ rt) (e := eTop.symm)
   852	  -- identify the target restriction map with `(eDf ∘ rt) ∘ eTop⁻¹`
   853	  convert step2 using 1 <;> try rfl
   854	  refine heq_of_eq ?_
   855	  apply LinearMap.ext; intro x
   856	  have hc := LinearMap.congr_fun hnathom (eTop.symm x)
   857	  simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at hc ⊢
   858	  refine (?_ : _ = _).trans hc.symm

   860	  exact (eTop.apply_symm_apply x).symm

   864	to the basic-open basis of `Spec R` (`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`): injectivity on stalks is

   866	`isIso_of_stalkFunctor_map_iso` concludes. Project-local glue used to assemble `IsIso M.fromTildeΓ`
   867	from per-basic-open section data. -/
   868	private theorem isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen {R : CommRingCat.{u}}
   869	    {F G : TopCat.Sheaf (ModuleCat.{u} R) (Spec R)} (α : F ⟶ G)
   870	    (h : ∀ f : R, IsIso (α.1.app (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)))) : IsIso α := by
   871	  have hB : TopologicalSpace.Opens.IsBasis (Set.range (@PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen R _)) :=
   872	    PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens
   873	  have hinj : ∀ U ∈ Set.range (@PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen R _),
   874	      Function.Injective (α.1.app (.op U)) := by
   875	    rintro U ⟨f, rfl⟩
   876	    exact ((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mp (h f)).1
   877	  have hstalk : ∀ x, IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) x).map α.1) := by
   878	    intro x
   879	    rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective]
   880	    refine ⟨TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis hB hinj x, ?_⟩
   881	    intro t
   882	    obtain ⟨U, hxU, hUB, s, rfl⟩ := TopCat.Presheaf.exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis hB G.presheaf x t
   883	    obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := hUB

   885	    exact ⟨F.presheaf.germ _ x hxU s', by rw [TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply]⟩
   886	  exact TopCat.Presheaf.isIso_of_stalkFunctor_map_iso α
   887	
   888	/-- A linear map intertwining two localizations of the same module at the same submonoid is
   889	bijective: if `f : M →ₗ M'` and `g : M →ₗ M''` both exhibit a localization at `S` and
   890	`h : M' →ₗ M''` satisfies `h ∘ₗ f = g`, then `h` is bijective (it is the canonical localization
   891	isomorphism `IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv`). Stated with the two `IsLocalizedModule` facts as
   892	explicit hypotheses to avoid typeclass-diamond ambiguity at the call site. -/
   893	private theorem bijective_comp_of_localizations {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : Submonoid R)
   894	    {M M' M'' : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
   895	    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M''] {f : M →ₗ[R] M'} {g : M →ₗ[R] M''} {h : M' →ₗ[R] M''}
   896	    (hf : IsLocalizedModule S f) (hg : IsLocalizedModule S g) (hh : h ∘ₗ f = g) :
   897	    Function.Bijective h := by
   898	  haveI := hf; haveI := hg
   899	  have heq : h = (IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv S f g).toLinearMap := by
   900	    apply IsLocalizedModule.linearMap_ext S (f := f) (f' := g)
   901	    apply LinearMap.ext
   902	    intro x
   903	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, hh,
   904	      LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap, IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv_apply]
   905	  rw [heq]
   906	  exact (IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv S f g).bijective
   907	
   908	/-- **`IsIso M.fromTildeΓ` from per-basic-open section localization** (the cheap stalk/section
   909	assembly of `lem:qcoh_affine_isIso_fromTildeΓ`, the blueprint "G1-assemble" step). If for every
   910	`f : R` the section restriction `Γ(M, ⊤) → Γ(M, D(f))` of a sheaf of modules `M` on `Spec R`
   911	exhibits the target as `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` over `R` — exactly the conclusion of G1-core
   912	(`lem:qcoh_affine_section_localization`,
   913	`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_isQuasicoherent`) — then the tilde-Gamma counit `M.fromTildeΓ` is
